reference.dump_args_comment: Dump ALL 16 encoder blocks, not the dumper's 6-block default (0,1,2,7,8,15). Added with the re-pin to the multilingual weights: blocks 10-13 carry a massive-activation channel (4) at |value| up to 344 while the rest of those tensors sit at p99 6-9, and BF16 drift peaks there (enc.block.12.out max_abs 3.1 on dots). Without these blocks the drift is only observable after the fact at enc.out. Same treatment as the -nc manifest.
reference.comment: First-party HF Transformers integration: granite_speech5_ctc / granite_speech5_encoder, GraniteSpeech5ForCTC, GraniteSpeech5FeatureExtractor and GraniteSpeech5Processor ship inside mainline transformers from v5.16 (dumped with 5.17.0). No trust_remote_code - config.json has no auto_map. The dumper mirrors the model card path: AutoProcessor + AutoModelForCTC + model.generate + processor.batch_decode(skip_special_tokens=True). attn_implementation=eager (GraniteSpeech5 sets _supports_flash_attn=False because the Shaw relative-position bias is a float attention mask). Pinned to the multilingual, cased and punctuated release (weights replaced upstream at 121ff64, 2026-10-21; the stale ctc_conformer remote code and preprocessor_config.json were removed at 621ff2e). The English-only weights were 18ca3c1.

oracle_dtype_comment: Weights ship BF16 and transformers' dtype='auto' would load BF16, but the dumps and the reference WER baseline are both taken at F32. The BF16->F32 upcast is lossless, so these are the shipped weights unchanged, and F32 activations over BF16 weights is exactly the transcribe.cpp compute regime. Measured on jfk: a BF16 forward gives an identical transcript and identical token ids, but tensors differ from F32 by up to 2-3% of p99_abs (enc.block.1.post_ff2 max |diff| = 0.44), which is ~250x the 1e-4 x p99_abs Stage 2 tolerance budget. A BF16 oracle would therefore force blind tolerance widening at Stage 4 and hide real implementation bugs.

frontend.comment: GraniteSpeech5FeatureExtractor. torchaudio.transforms.MelSpectrogram(sr=16000, n_fft=512, win_length=400, hop_length=160, n_mels=80) at library defaults: power=2.0, Hann PERIODIC, center=True, pad_mode=reflect, f_min=0, f_max=8000, mel_scale=htk, norm=None (UNNORMALIZED triangular filters, not Slaney). win_length=400 != n_fft=512, so the window is zero-padded to 512 inside the STFT. Then clamp_min(1e-10) -> log10 -> per-utterance floor at (global max over BOTH time and mel bins) - 8.0 -> fixed affine x/4 + 1. That normalization is bit-for-bit src/transcribe-mel.cpp's existing per_utterance mode ((x+4)/4); it is a dynamic-range floor, NOT CMVN. Then concat torchaudio.functional.compute_deltas(win_length=3) along the channel axis (80 -> 160) and stack 2 consecutive frames (160 -> 320). FRAMING: mel_frames = n_samples // 160; num_frames = 2*ceil(mel_frames/2); the WAVEFORM is right-padded to (num_frames-1)*160+1 samples; the melspec is sliced to [..., :num_frames]. For even mel_frames this drops one trailing center-pad frame; for odd mel_frames it keeps it. The trailing partial stacking group is VALID, not masked: encoder_frame_counts = ceil(mel_frames/2) equals the emitted frame count (verified valid=550/550 on jfk, 1767/1767 on dots).

tokenizer_summary.comment: SentencePiece-derived BPE with byte fallback (same tokenizer family as the -nc sibling; the English-only revision 18ca3c1 shipped GPT-2 byte-level BPE). Decoder: Replace(U+2581 -> ' '), ByteFallback, Fuse, Strip(1 leading space). Vocab carries cased pieces and punctuation. <unk> at id 0 is simultaneously the CTC blank, pad_token_id and unk_token. Ids 1..254 are special added tokens (<|nospeech|>, <pad>, <|endoftext|>, <|startoftranscript|>, ..., <|spltokenN|>) that the reference drops via batch_decode(skip_special_tokens=True); the converter types them CONTROL and the runtime drops them too. Ids 255..510 are <0x00>..<0xFF> byte-fallback pieces. No language tokens: the model has no language conditioning. tokenizer_class=ParakeetTokenizer, whose _decode does the CTC groupby-then-drop-pad collapse.

capabilities.comment: Multilingual (en, fr, de, es, pt, it, ja per the model card) cased and punctuated encoder-CTC with no language conditioning, no language identification output and no timestamp surface. CTC emission frames do not provide trustworthy word durations, and upstream publishes no alignment reference, so segment, word, and token timestamp requests are unsupported. Upstream publishes benchmarks only as bar-chart images; the model card states 5.51% average Open ASR leaderboard English WER for this release (5.78% for the English-only one). Stage 4 and Stage 7 gate against the measured Oracle reference baseline on LibriSpeech test-clean - see reports/wer/granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc-REF.test-clean.{jsonl,score.json}.

cases_comment: jfk has mel_frames=1100 (even) and dots has mel_frames=3533 (odd). The two parities are different code paths in the feature extractor: the odd case right-pads the waveform and keeps the trailing center-pad frame, the even case drops it. dots (35.3 s) also spans many more 128-frame attention blocks than jfk (11.0 s).
